The statement says the Service may, by notice, appoint any person, including a non-resident supplier, to collect and remit VAT. The passage (section 158) only covers taxable persons implementing the fiscalisation system and describes what that system may include; it says nothing about appointing collection agents, notices, or non-resident suppliers.

The statement that a small company's return may contain a statement of accounts attested by the taxpayer in place of audited financial statements is not stated in the passages, which cover company return filing times, cessation filings, and designated representatives only.

The statement says the rule does not apply to distributions by a real estate investment company from rental and dividend income received on behalf of shareholders, whether from current or previous periods' profits. The passage (section 7) defines Nigerian dividends and says nothing about real estate investment companies, rental income, or any exclusion for them.

Collection of the tax stays in abeyance until the objection or appeal is determined, when notice of objection or appeal has been given. The passage only defines 'dispute' as a disagreement on interpretation of facts or law arising from an assessment, action or decision; it says nothing about notice, objection or appeal procedure, or suspension of collection.

The statement's rule that a relevant tax authority may adjust a non-arm's length related-party arrangement under the Transfer Pricing Regulations is not stated in the passages. The only passage gives the definition of "tax" and says nothing about transfer pricing, arm's length arrangements, related parties, or adjustments.
